title: A latent chain with sixteen states, decoded to one state per token
summary: A hidden chain moves between k = 16 latent states with fixed move probabilities, and each latent state has its own probability table over symbols. While reading, the model keeps a single latent state: after each symbol it moves to the successor that best explains that symbol, and it predicts the symbol the next latent state most probably produces.
core_idea: Track text with one of sixteen latent states, moving to the best successor at every symbol.

state.name: z
state.meaning: Index of the current latent state, one of k = 16; the only thing carried between tokens, so the carried information is log2 16 = 4 bits.

update.name: move
update.plain: z_t = argmax over j of A[z_prev, j] * B[j, x_t]; A is the k by k move table, B the k by V symbol table

readout.name: predict
readout.plain: y_hat = argmax over v of sum_j A[z_t, j] * B[j, v]

learning.description: A and B are estimated from counts: decode the training text to latent states with the current tables, count moves and symbols per state, normalize, repeat.
learning.few_shot_argument: The tables have k^2 + kV entries and are set from counts, so a rule that fits in 16 states is learned from a few hundred examples; this card states 400 examples for copying at L = 2.

cost.why: The complexity claim is stated in n, k and V; the width of the tables is the number of states.

copy.why: Sixteen states whatever the size: the carried state is one index, 4 bits.

resources.why: k = 16 states, decoded to one state per token, so the carried state holds log2 16 = 4 bits.

limits.resources: the carried state z, one of k = 16 latent states (4 bits), at any task size
limits.why: Two-type bracket prefixes at depth D have 2^D different stacks of open brackets. Two prefixes with different stacks that leave the same state get the same predictions on every continuation, but closing the first stack reaches a level where the two stacks differ and the legal closer differs, so one prediction is wrong. Exact prediction at depth D needs at least 2^D distinct states; 2^5 = 32 > 16 states, so the chain fails from depth 5 on.

complexity.constants_notes: Per token: k products and k - 1 comparisons for the move, k V products and V - 1 comparisons for the prediction. The carried state is one index.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Count-based estimates of a small table. Example counts m this card states for its learning rule at the solvable cases, each reaching 0.99 on three seeds: 400 for copying at L = 2, 400 for recall at K = 2, 300 for bracket nesting at depth 2 and 400 for two-hop lookup at table size 2. Information account for each count, one target-rule class per task (m counts whole training instances, each with all its scored answers). Copying at L = 2. Class definition: every selector s from the output indices {0, 1} to the source positions {0, 1}; the rule answers at output index i with the source symbol at position s(i), and the target is s(i) = i. Size justification: each of the 2 output indices has 2 choices, so |H| = 2^2 = 4; two different selectors differ at some index i, and a source string with different symbols at the two selected positions gives them different answers. log2 |H| = 2. Recall at K = 2. Class definition: the K stored pairs sorted by the id of their first token as k_0 < k_1, with second tokens v_0, v_1 (the sorting only names the pairs; the input keeps its shuffled order); every selector s from {0, 1} to {0, 1}; the rule answers a request for k_i with v_s(i), and the target is s(i) = i. Size justification: each of the 2 ranks has 2 choices, so |H| = 2^2 = 4; two different selectors differ at some rank, and pairs with different second tokens at the two selected ranks give them different answers. log2 |H| = 2. Bracket nesting at depth 2. Class definition: the six nonempty stack contexts (0), (1), (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), listed bottom to top; every map from these contexts to the two closing tokens, evaluated after each scored prefix; the target maps a context to the closer of its top bracket. Size justification: two choices for each of six contexts, so |H| = 2^6 = 64; all six contexts occur in valid depth-2 prefixes, so different maps give different answers there. log2 |H| = 6. Two-hop lookup at table size 2. Class definition: every selector s from {0, 1} to {0, 1}; given the tables g and f in the input and the request x, the rule answers f(g(s(x))), and the target is s(x) = x. Size justification: each of the 2 requests has 2 choices, so |H| = 2^2 = 4; when two selectors differ at some x, tables g and f that send the two selected arguments to different outputs give them different answers. log2 |H| = 2. Prior bits: 0, relative to these declared classes: the task protocol supplies the token encoding and the restriction to each class, and the mechanism receives no hand-set member of it. This is a restricted-class information bound, not a claim that learning the parsing or lookup operation is free. Bits per example (one whole instance): at most 4 for copying (2 answers over 4 symbols), 8 for recall (2 answers over 16 symbols), 7 for bracket nesting (7 scored closers of one bit), and 2 for two-hop lookup (2 answers over 2 symbols). The account assumes a target drawn uniformly from each class, so it bounds m from below only; the counts m above are this card's stated claim and are not derived from it.

prediction.statement: 400 copy examples at L = 2 over 4 symbols give per-string accuracy 0.99.

capabilities.prediction: Exact up to depth log2 16 = 4; deeper prefixes need at least 2^D distinct states to know the legal closer, so accuracy falls below 0.99 at depth 8 and 16; at depth 16 per-sequence accuracy is at most 16 / 2^16.
Fails once the tables given in context hold more than 4 bits, which is already the case at the listed table sizes 4, 16 and 32.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: Exact only while L log2 D is at most 4 bits; fails at the listed lengths 8 to 64, where per-string accuracy is at most 16 / D^L (16 / 4^64 at L = 64 over 4 symbols).
Exact only while K log2 V is at most 4 bits; fails at the listed K of 8 to 64; at K = 64 over 16 symbols per-query accuracy is at chance, 1/16.

falsifiers: A configuration with 16 states predicts the legal closer at depth 8 with accuracy at least 0.99.
The carried state after a token needs more than one integer index.

toy_example.description: A two-state version decoding four symbols and scoring the next symbol.
toy_example.python:
import json
A = [[0.7, 0.3], [0.4, 0.6]]
B = [[0.9, 0.1], [0.2, 0.8]]
z = 0
path = []
for x in [1, 1, 0, 1]:
    scores = [A[z][j] * B[j][x] for j in range(2)]
    z = max(range(2), key=lambda j: scores[j])
    path.append(z)
nxt = [sum(A[z][j] * B[j][v] for j in range(2)) for v in range(2)]
print(json.dumps({"final_state": z, "states_visited": sum(path), "next_symbol_score_1": round(nxt[1], 9)},
                 sort_keys=True))
